SELECTED_INDEX: 2  
CONFIDENCE: 0.25  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows no C=O band near 1700 cm⁻¹, excluding candidates that contain carbonyl groups (e.g., 1).  A very strong C–H stretching envelope appears at 2942 cm⁻¹ with additional components at 2845 cm⁻¹ and 2796–2720 cm⁻¹, typical of long, saturated alkyl chains and the aldehydic-type C–H Fermi pair near 2720–2830 cm⁻¹.  Candidate 2 (COCCCCCC=S) is the only molecule that combines a long straight alkyl chain (accounts for the intense CH₂/CH₃ bands at 1467 and 1307 cm⁻¹ and the CH stretches) with a terminal C=S (thio-carbonyl) group whose ν(C=S) Raman band normally falls around 1020–1150 cm⁻¹, matching the observed peaks at 1017 and 1045 cm⁻¹.  The C–S single-bond stretch often appears near 500–550 cm⁻¹, consistent with the 515 cm⁻¹ band.  No other candidate provides this combination of alkyl, C–O (1130 cm⁻¹) and thiocarbonyl (≈1030 cm⁻¹) features while lacking a C=O stretch.  Hence candidate 2 best fits the observed Raman data.
